about: Fragment selection for the trace workflow. Its required set in step-01 is short and stack-neutral, which makes over-loading the interesting failure here rather than under-loading.

cases.name: Traceability for a Go service with no JavaScript anywhere
cases.prompt: Map the acceptance criteria for the settlement epic onto the existing tests and tell me which criteria have no coverage.
repoFacts: Go module with *_test.go files; there is no package.json anywhere in the repo
no browser automation, no pact artifacts, no .maestro directory

assertions.text: Both library flags are true and neither package can be installed in a repo with no JavaScript manifest, so both mandates stay closed. A Go repo is where a flag-only reading of the run-level preconditions does the most damage, because there is no manifest the agent could even inspect.

Traceability is a mapping problem, not a framework problem. The required set is the same five fragments whatever the stack, and pulling in browser or contract fragments because the epic mentions an API is over-loading.

cases.name: Traceability for a mobile epic with Maestro flows present
cases.prompt: Map the onboarding epic's acceptance criteria onto our device flows and unit tests, and produce the gate decision.
repoFacts: Expo app; .maestro/ contains eight flow files
jest unit tests alongside the app source

assertions.text: The presence of Maestro flows changes what is being traced, not which fragments the trace workflow needs. Its step file names no mobile branch, so adding maestro-flows here would be inventing a rule the workflow does not have.
